transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-19
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Mendez (Redwood SE), Laura Chen (Head of Search, Orbit Cloud), Marcus Lee (ML Engineer), Priya Singh (CTO)

Summary (auto):
High-level discovery on Orbit Cloud's search stack and plan to evaluate embeddings + reranking. Customer is exploring hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment for privacy and throughput. Interest in hybrid search (BM25 + vector rerank), HNSW params/tuning, dimensionality tradeoffs, and integration with their existing vector DB (currently evaluating Milvus and Pinecone). Action items: share pricing, security docs, and schedule benchmark with sample dataset.

Transcript:
[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Samira from Redwood, AE on the account, and with me is Diego, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:05] Laura: Hey Samira, thanks. I'm Laura. Good. We'll kick off — thanks for setting this up.
[00:08] Priya: Hi all, Priya here. I'm going to listen in, high level.
[00:12] Marcus: Marcus — I'm on the search infra team.
[00:15] Samira: Awesome. Quick agenda — understand current stack, goals for embeddings + rerank, constraints (security, latency, cost), and next steps. Sound good?
[00:21] Laura: Yep. Short background: Orbit Cloud provides multi-tenant logs and metrics search to our customers. We're doing keyword search today with OpenSearch/BM25. We're seeing limitations with semantic queries and want to add embeddings+reranking to improve recall for fuzzy queries. We're evaluating hosted options and also dedicated/private because a bunch of customers need data residency and stricter controls.
[00:40] Diego: Thanks Laura. Are you planning to use a separate vector DB or store vectors alongside OpenSearch? What's the integration surface?
[00:47] Marcus: Good question. We're piloting Milvus and Pinecone. Two patterns we're considering: 1) keep text index in OpenSearch and do a hybrid search where BM25 returns top-200 then vector rerank, or 2) full-vector by storing vectors in a vector DB and doing ANN search then cross-encoder rerank. We want to compare latency and cost.
[01:08] Samira: Great — both are common. For hybrid often people do BM25->vector rerank for latency/cost balance. Redwood can host embeddings model and also provide reranking models (we have small cross-encoder variants). For deployment mode: hosted gives fastest time-to-value, dedicated gives predictability for throughput and VPC options, private gives full control for air-gapped/residency.
[01:30] Priya: Our main constraints: sub-200ms p95 for interactive UI, sustained 300 QPS during peak indexing periods, and SOC2/SAML requirements. Also, we need to keep vectors encrypted at rest with customer-managed keys.
[01:48] Diego: We support KMS integrations and can work with customer-managed keys in Dedicated/Private deployments; hosted also supports encryption but with Redwood-managed keys by default — we can share SOC2 docs.
[01:58] Laura: Perfect — can you share what models you recommend for embeddings (dimensionality)? We're seeing 1536 dims from some providers and 512 from others.
[02:07] Diego: Yeah — dimensionality tradeoffs are key. Higher dims like 1536 usually give better accuracy for some models but increase storage and nearest-neighbor compute. 512 or 768 are common sweet spots. If you're using HNSW in Milvus/Pinecone, memory and index size scale roughly linearly with dimension. Also quantization like PQ or OPQ can help reduce RAM. For reranking we recommend a two-stage approach: sparse retrieval (BM25), dense ANN to get top-k (e.g., 200), then a cross-encoder reranker over the top-20. That reduces cross-encoder cost and improves final relevance.
[02:45] Marcus: For us, storage is a concern because we have ~10M docs and 800 GB of text. If we pick 1536 dims that's a lot. Do you have rough numbers for storage and cost?
[02:55] Samira: Quick ballpark: uncompressed float32 at 1536 dims is ~6 KB per vector; at 512 dims ~2 KB. So 10M vectors at 1536 ~60 GB, actually sorry, check math — 1536 * 4 bytes = 6144 bytes ~6 KB -> times 10M ~60 GB? Wait that's 60 GB * 10? Let me recalc: 6 KB * 10M = 60 GB, yes. So it's ~60 GB raw, but indexing overhead and HNSW graph and replication add overhead — typical on-disk+RAM may be 3x depending on settings. With quantization you can get to <1 KB per vector.
[03:30] Marcus: That helps. We care about QPS and latency too — do you have guidance on batching/throughput when serving embeddings from Redwood hosted vs dedicated?
[03:38] Diego: Hosted is multitenant and has good throughput but less predictable for high sustained QPS. For predictable sustained throughput and V100/A100 pools we recommend Dedicated. Typically you can get >500 small-embedding QPS from a single Dedicated worker depending on model and batching. We can also tune batch sizes and latency SLOs. For reranker cross-encoders those are heavier — you'll want GPUs with enough memory or CPU inference for small scales.
[04:00] Laura: We're also exploring using Redwood's embeddings model vs OpenAI or open-source models. Anything special about Redwood embeddings?
[04:07] Samira: Redwood offers curated open models and verified performance profiles. In many cases open models (e.g., open embeddings from community) are cost-effective; we can run side-by-side evaluations on quality and cost. We also provide streaming and consistent API across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
[04:20] Priya: Security: SOC2, SAML, audit logs, tenant isolation — can Dedicated satisfy our compliance?
[04:26] Diego: Yes, Dedicated gives tenant isolation and optional network-level controls (VPC peering, dedicated subnets). For maximum compliance we recommend Private deployment, but Dedicated hits a lot of enterprise needs with SLAs and isolation. We can share our security whitepaper and SOC2 report — we'll attach that after.
[04:42] Marcus: How about vector DB vendor support — we currently have engineers familiar with Milvus but Pinecone is attractive for managed ops. Does Redwood plug into both easily?
[04:52] Samira: Yes — Redwood exposes embeddings via API; you can push vectors to any vector DB. We also have connectors and community examples for Milvus, Pinecone, and OpenSearch dense vector fields. For reranking you can either call Redwood's reranker endpoint after ANN or run a hosted reranker co-located with the vector DB in your VPC for low latency.
[05:12] Laura: One thing we worry about: cold-start latency and prefix caching. When artifacts are not warm, the first few queries spike latency. How do you handle that?
[05:20] Diego: We do KV cache and automatic warmup for common prefixes on Dedicated; you can also pin models to keep them resident. On hosted, we have warming heuristics but less guarantee. For strict p95 SLOs Dedicated allows pinning and reserved capacity.
[05:34] Priya: Marcus, do we have a target latency for reranker stage?
[05:37] Marcus: End-to-end for UI we want p95 < 200ms. That means the reranker step has to be sub-100ms ideally. Doing cross-encoder on top-20 might be tight without optimized infra.
[05:49] Diego: That's why folks do a smaller top-k for expensive cross-encoders or use distilled rerankers. We can also do a two-tier rerank: a lighter scoring model first then full cross-encoder for small set. Also quantized int8 cross-encoders help on GPU.
[06:06] Laura: On integration, what telemetry and tracing do you provide so we can debug relevance regressions?
[06:12] Samira: Redwood Console provides per-route latency, token-level cost, and tracing hooks. You can see top queries, rollout comparisons, and link to eval sets to detect regressions. We can export logs to your SIEM and provide per-request IDs for correlation.
[06:27] Marcus: Does Redwood support hybrid search out of the box or we need to glue it?
[06:31] Diego: We don't operate your vector DB; Redwood provides embeddings + reranker APIs. Hybrid glue is usually done on the app side: call OpenSearch for BM25, call ANN provider for dense results, then call Redwood reranker. We do have SDK examples and a hybrid example in the docs that show how to orchestrate.
[06:47] Laura: Could you show a rough architecture for dedicated/private?
[06:50] Diego: Sure — (Diego screenshares briefly) — For Dedicated: we run a Redwood-managed control plane and a dedicated inference pool in your cloud account or our cluster depending on option, VPC peering, KMS integration, and optional private control plane. For Private: full on-prem or VPC-hosted stack with customer-managed networking.
[07:10] Priya: When you say dedicated inference pool, are GPUs colocated with our data? We want to avoid egress of raw logs.
[07:17] Diego: You can configure VPC peering and private networking so inference happens within your network and logs do not leave. For on-prem Private deployment, you'd keep everything in your datacenter.
[07:26] Laura: About benchmarking — we'd like to run a performance test: 10k queries, 200 QPS, hybrid BM25->dense->rerank. Can Redwood run that for us on Dedicated?
[07:36] Samira: Yes, Diego can prepare the harness. We'll need your sample dataset and example queries. We'll propose a config and run it in a dedicated environment.
[07:44] Marcus: Ok we'll get that sample data to you. One more: how do you handle versioning and rollouts for models (we're worried about quality regressions)?
[07:52] Diego: Redwood has model pinning and rollout policies — canaries, A/B, and automatic fallback. You can tie regressions to eval sets and block a rollout if metrics drop. Console shows diffed metrics for prompt sets.
[08:04] Priya: Cost: can you ballpark embeddings cost per 1M vectors for hosted vs dedicated?
[08:09] Samira: Ballpark: hosted embeddings (managed) is higher per embedding but you pay only for usage. Dedicated involves a monthly committed cost but unit embedding cost drops significantly for high volume. Exact numbers vary so we'll share a pricing sheet.
[08:20] Laura: Competitors — we looked at Pinecone and Vectara; Vectara touts end-to-end managed retrieval/rerank. Why Redwood vs them?
[08:29] Diego: Redwood positions for production-grade inference and flexible deployment modes. We focus on cost controls (batching, caching, quantization), rollout controls, and predictable Dedicated capacity. Vectara is end-to-end but may be less flexible on private deployments; Pinecone is solid for managed ANN but you still need reranker glue.
[08:47] Marcus: Any gotchas with HNSW params? We've seen recalls drop when efConstruction or efSearch are too low.
[08:55] Diego: Yes — efConstruction affects index build recall vs build time; efSearch and M impact query recall/latency. We'll share recommended defaults (efConstruction ~200-500 for large indexes, M 16-64 depending on recall/ram). For real-time updates, HNSW reinsert costs matter. For heavy write workloads you might tune differently.
[09:12] Laura: Do you support on-the-fly embedding updates when documents change?
[09:16] Samira: Yes — typical flow: on doc update compute embedding and upsert to vector DB. For Dedicated you can co-locate embedding compute to reduce egress.
[09:23] Marcus: Index maintenance — reindex strategy for new embedding model — how do you recommend?
[09:27] Diego: Common approach: run offline re-embed job, create new index/namespace, run A/B traffic split, then cutover. Redwood supports pinned model versions so you can keep old traffic on older embeddings during migration.
[09:40] Laura: Are there limits on dimensionality in your runtime? For example custom 4096-dim vectors?
[09:45] Diego: We can host large dims but it's less common; dimension itself is fine but memory/latency/cost scale. Many vector DBs cap certain sizes or recommend quantization. We'll run a test if you want 4096.
[09:56] Marcus: For reranking models, can we host our own cross-encoder in Dedicated?
[10:00] Samira: Yes — you can bring your own model artifacts. Dedicated and Private allow you to deploy custom models, and we provide the runtime to host them with inference APIs.
[10:08] Priya: Integration dependencies — do you have SDKs or examples for Java/Go?
[10:12] Samira: Yes we have SDKs in Python, Node, Java, Go. We'll attach links in the follow-up.
[10:18] Laura: Regarding observability, does Redwood emit per-request traces to Jaeger/Datadog?
[10:23] Diego: We can export traces and logs to your observability stack; Console also has native dashboards.
[10:28] Marcus: Any recommendations for index sharding across regions? We have users in EU and NA.
[10:33] Diego: Many customers maintain region-local indexes for latency, then replicate metadata or use global routing. Redwood routing can send queries to region-local pools and fallback to another region if needed.
[10:43] Laura: Security again — do you offer per-tenant encryption keys or is it per-account?
[10:48] Diego: We support customer-managed keys via KMS and can scope keys to environment. For multi-tenant explicit tenant isolation is recommended on Dedicated/Private.
[10:57] Samira: Quick note — we'll attach our SOC2, the security whitepaper, and an architecture sketch after the call.
[11:02] Marcus: Good. For the benchmark, target environment? GPU type?
[11:06] Diego: We recommend A10/A100 for dense encoders; for embeddings A10 or T4 often suffice. We'll propose both.
[11:12] Laura: Who will be the main contacts? Marcus for infra, me for product, Priya for exec.
[11:17] Samira: Great — Samira will own the commercial side, Diego will run the tech bench.
[11:21] Priya: Timeline — we want a pilot in September and decision by Oct. Is that doable?
[11:26] Samira: Yes that timeline aligns; we'll try to get the benchmark next week and pricing the week after.
[11:31] Laura: One more operational question: retention and deletion — can Redwood support deletion webhooks for vectors when customers exercise data deletion?
[11:38] Diego: Yes — you can orchestrate deletes via our APIs; Dedicated/Private gives you more control to ensure no copies persist.
[11:44] Marcus: On the billing side, do you have overage protections or hard caps?
[11:48] Samira: We support quota controls and can set caps for hosted; Dedicated is committed capacity so terms vary. We'll include options.
[11:55] Laura: Ok, let's recap next steps.
[11:58] Samira: Recap: Samira to send pricing and security docs; Diego to prepare benchmark harness and HNSW recommendations; Orbit to send sample dataset and queries; schedule benchmark next Tue (proposed 2025-08-26)/time TBD.
[12:12] Priya: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[12:15] Marcus: Thanks.
[12:17] Samira: Thanks all — we'll follow up with links and a calendar invite.
